finding.claim: The /fetch handler passes the `target` query parameter straight to http.Get. There is no scheme or host validation and no redirect restriction. An unauthenticated caller can make the server request internal hosts, loopback services, or the cloud metadata endpoint (169.254.169.254). The response body is copied back to the caller (full-read SSRF). Severity: HIGH.
finding.sink: http.Get(target) at main.go:16; the response body is returned to the caller by io.Copy(w, resp.Body) at main.go:22

trace.note: http.Get(target) uses the unvalidated value as the full URL. The default client follows redirects.
io.Copy(w, resp.Body) returns the fetched content to the attacker
Handler registered at /fetch with no auth middleware

finding.guards_checked: No allowlist, scheme check, or IP/CIDR blocking on the path. No auth middleware is registered. http.Get uses the default client, which follows redirects with no CheckRedirect. The `allowed` map is only consulted in safeFetch, not in fetch. The handler is not an intentional user-configured proxy (no DEPLOY-REC exemption).

verdict.reason: main.go:15-16 passes the query param `target` directly to http.Get with no validation, main.go:22 copies the response body back to the caller, and main.go:41 registers /fetch with no auth; the `allowed` check exists only in safeFetch (main.go:27).
